name: Salesforce
one_liner: Enterprise CRM platform offering a broad REST API and official Hosted MCP Servers for managing Salesforce records, Flows, Apex actions, and analytics.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 (Web Server with PKCE, Client Credentials, Refresh Token, and JWT Bearer flows) issuing Bearer access tokens; creating Connected Apps is restricted as of Spring '26 in favor of External Client Apps.
access_notes: Developers can use free Developer Edition orgs with API access enabled by default, while production API access requires Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, or Professional (with paid API add-on), and Hosted MCP Servers require Flex Credits.
api_surface_notes: Covers SObject CRUD operations, Apex REST, Invocable Actions, @AuraEnabled methods, Flows, Named Queries, Data 360 SQL, Tableau analytics, and Prompt Builder templates; rate limits are not detailed in retrieved docs.
primary_blocker: Complex enterprise OAuth setup (External Client Apps replacing Connected Apps in Spring '26), production API gating on lower tiers, and Hosted MCP requiring Flex Credits plus per-org admin activation.

name: HubSpot
one_liner: HubSpot is a CRM and sales platform offering broad REST APIs and an official remote MCP server to read and manage CRM records, activities, conversations, and marketing assets.
auth_notes: Multi-account apps require OAuth2 (30-minute Bearer access tokens with refresh tokens; OAuth 2.1 with PKCE required for the remote MCP server; client_credentials used for the webhooks journal API). Single-account integrations can use static auth Bearer tokens or scoped service keys, while select endpoints (e.g., custom channels) use a developer API key via the hapikey query parameter.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve create HubSpot accounts, OAuth apps, service keys, and MCP connectors for free without sales approval. Private OAuth apps are capped at 10 allowlisted accounts, public HubSpot Marketplace listing (including MCP server components) requires Ecosystem Quality review, installing apps requires Super Admin or Marketplace Access permissions, and certain advanced objects/features require paid Hub tiers.
api_surface_notes: Covers CRM records (contacts, companies, deals, tickets, leads, line items, quotes, invoices, orders, carts, products, subscriptions, custom objects, segments), activities (calls, emails, meetings, notes, tasks), marketing/CMS content, conversations/custom channels, pipelines, properties, and webhooks. Combined limit of 100 project-based apps, service keys, and MCP connectors per account; Sensitive Data settings block conversation and activity access on the MCP server (though not standard CRM APIs).
primary_blocker: None

name: Pipedrive
one_liner: Pipedrive is a CRM and sales pipeline management platform for tracking deals, leads, contacts, organizations, and sales activities.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 (via oauth.pipedrive.com with HTTP Basic Auth on client_id/client_secret for token exchange; 60-minute access tokens and 60-day inactivity expiry on refresh tokens) and single-user API tokens passed in the x-api-token header.
access_notes: Developers can request a Developer Sandbox Account self-serve via Developer Hub to create public or private OAuth apps and obtain client credentials; submitting a public app to the Pipedrive Marketplace requires approval.
api_surface_notes: RESTful JSON API (v1 and v2) covering the majority of core CRM functionality including deals, persons, organizations, leads, activities, products, pipelines/stages, notes, synced email threads, and projects. Official OpenAPI 3 specs are published for both v1 and v2; webhooks and rate limits are not detailed in the provided evidence.
primary_blocker: None

name: Attio
one_liner: Attio is a modern CRM platform for managing people, companies, deals, custom objects, lists, tasks, notes, and communications.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow (workspace-level with optional PKCE or user-level with required PKCE) and single-workspace API keys; tokens do not expire and are sent as Bearer tokens (or HTTP Basic Auth with the token as username).
access_notes: API keys and Attio MCP are available self-serve on all plans. Developers can register OAuth apps self-serve in the developer console, with unpublished apps installable in up to 25 workspaces before requiring an approved release.
api_surface_notes: Public JSON REST API at https://api.attio.com/v2/ covering objects, records, attributes, lists, tasks, notes, views, comments, activities, emails, meetings, call recordings, user management, and webhooks; rate limits match 100 req/s (read), 25 req/s (write), and 5 req/s (merge).
primary_blocker: None for single-workspace API keys, up to 25 OAuth workspace installs, or Attio's official MCP server; scaling a shared OAuth app beyond 25 workspaces requires an approved app release.

name: Twenty
one_liner: Twenty is an open-source CRM platform for managing companies, people, opportunities, custom objects, and workflows across cloud and self-hosted workspaces.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code with PKCE, Client Credentials, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, and api/profile scopes) as well as role-scoped API keys passed as Bearer tokens.
access_notes: Self-serve signup via app.twenty.com (CAPTCHA-protected web onboarding) or self-hosted open-source deployment; API keys are generated in Settings and OAuth clients register dynamically via API without manual review.
api_surface_notes: Core API (/rest/, /graphql/) covers CRUD on People, Companies, Opportunities, and custom objects; Metadata API (/rest/metadata/, /metadata/) manages schemas. Endpoints and OpenAPI specs (/rest/open-api/core, /rest/open-api/metadata) are generated per workspace schema; supports 60-record batches and 100 req/min rate limit.
primary_blocker: None

name: Podio
one_liner: Podio is a customizable collaborative workspace, CRM, and project management platform for organizing teams, apps, items, tasks, and workflows.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth2 (server-side, client-side, username/password, and single-app authentication flows) with self-serve Client ID and Client Secret; access tokens expire in 8 hours, refresh tokens in 28 days, and requests use the Authorization: OAuth2 ACCESS_TOKEN header.
access_notes: Both free and paid Podio accounts have full self-serve API access and can generate Client ID/Secret keys in account settings; higher rate limits require a paid API Add-on, and elevated client trust levels (for destructive deletes) or programmatic app token retrieval require contacting support.
api_surface_notes: Covers 40+ documented API areas including Items, Applications, Spaces, Organizations, Tasks, Comments, Files, Contacts, Search, Views, Batch, Flows, and Hooks; subject to Limit A (250 calls/hour for resource-intensive ops) and Limit B (1,000 calls/hour standard) unless upgraded via API Add-on.
primary_blocker: None

name: Zoho CRM
one_liner: Zoho CRM is a cloud CRM and sales platform for managing leads, contacts, accounts, deals, workflows, and custom business modules.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow (web-based and self-client) and Self-Client Credentials flow, issuing organization-specific tokens tied to Production, Sandbox, or Developer environments with domain-specific accounts and API servers; access tokens expire in 1 hour and refresh tokens have unlimited lifetime until revoked.
access_notes: Developers can register web-based or self-client apps in the Zoho Developer/API Console using a Zoho CRM account (with Production, Sandbox, or Developer environments) without sales approval or app review; MCP and API requests consume organization API credit limits.
api_surface_notes: V8 REST APIs cover Core CRUD across standard and custom modules (Leads, Contacts, Accounts, Deals, Campaigns, Tasks, Invoices, etc.), Metadata APIs (modules, fields, layouts, related lists), Bulk APIs, COQL queries, Composite API (up to 5 calls per request), and settings/users/org endpoints; OAS files are generic and require fetching module metadata for custom business logic.
primary_blocker: None

name: Close
one_liner: Close is a CRM and sales engagement platform for managing leads, contacts, opportunities, tasks, communications, and sales workflows.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with rotating refresh tokens (all.full_access and offline_access scopes) and OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration for MCP, as well as user-scoped API keys sent via HTTP Basic Auth (API key as username, empty password) or Close-API-Key/Close-Scope headers on MCP.
access_notes: Developers can create API keys and Private OAuth apps self-serve, and existing OAuth apps continue working even if a Close subscription expires. However, OAuth apps are Private to one organization by default and require requesting Close approval to make public for multi-customer authorization, and non-customers must email support@close.com to request a free Dev organization.
api_surface_notes: REST API at https://api.close.com/api/v1 covers leads, contacts, opportunities, custom objects, tasks, activities (email, calls, SMS, WhatsApp, meetings, notes), pipelines, statuses, templates, Smart Views, users, roles, and workflows; supports _skip/_limit and cursor pagination, _fields filtering, partial PUT updates, and 429 rate-limit handling.
primary_blocker: Multi-customer OAuth apps are Private by default and require requesting public app approval from Close, non-customers must email support@close.com for a free Dev org, and the official OpenAPI spec (https://api.close.com/api/openapi.json) is experimental with incomplete schema coverage.

name: Copper
one_liner: Copper is a CRM and sales platform for managing clients, leads, contacts, pipelines, deals, tasks, and activities.
auth_notes: Supports legacy API Keys (passed via X-PW-AccessToken, X-PW-UserEmail, and X-PW-Application: developer_api headers) and OAuth2.0 Authorization Code Grant (Bearer tokens that currently do not expire and use a single broad scope developer/v1/all).
access_notes: API keys are generated in-app under System settings > API Keys by Copper workspace users/admins (no standalone free developer sandbox is documented). Third-party OAuth2.0 integrations must manually email partners@copper.com to register an app and obtain client_id and client_secret.
api_surface_notes: JSON REST API at https://api.copper.com/developer_api/v1/ covering most Copper resources (account, leads, deals, tasks, activities, search, and bulk APIs). Rate limits are 180 requests/min rolling window and 3 requests/sec for bulk APIs; TLS 1.2+ required. Official MCP is currently a waitlist/read-only Claude-only beta.
primary_blocker: OAuth2.0 app registration requires manual partner outreach to partners@copper.com for client_id and client_secret, and there is no documented self-serve developer sandbox (API keys require an active Copper account); official MCP is still waitlist-only and read-only for Claude.

name: DealCloud
one_liner: DealCloud is an enterprise CRM and deal management platform for tracking relationships, pipelines, and deal workflows.
auth_notes: REST API uses the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow, exchanging a client_id and user-enabled API key (as client_secret) for a 900-second Bearer token. Official DealCloud MCP uses OAuth 2.0 with .well-known dynamic discovery for per-user sign-in.
access_notes: No self-serve developer sandbox or free trial is documented. API keys require an enterprise DealCloud tenant with admin or CSM-enabled user group API permissions; MCP requires a DealCloud Celeste license, and custom or third-party AI clients require contacting a DealCloud Account Manager.
api_surface_notes: Covers User Management (v1), Data (v4), Schema (v4), Publications (v1), Relationship Intelligence Import (v1), and Site Backups (v4), plus an official Python SDK. Each tenant hosts an interactive Swagger UI at https://{{host}}/swagger; rate limits and sandbox details are not documented in retrieved excerpts.
primary_blocker: No self-serve developer sandbox or trial; requires an enterprise DealCloud tenant with admin/CSM-provisioned API permissions, plus Celeste licensing and Account Manager approval for third-party MCP integrations.

name: Zendesk
one_liner: Zendesk is a customer support and helpdesk platform for managing support tickets, users, organizations, help center content, and automated workflows.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code flow with optional PKCE and Client Credentials flow) using short-lived Bearer tokens and granular scopes. Multi-customer integrations require a Zendesk-approved Global OAuth client. Basic Auth via email/token API tokens is deprecated, with unused tokens deactivating starting July 28, 2026 and full removal by April 30, 2027.
access_notes: Single-instance OAuth clients can be created by a Zendesk admin in Admin Center or via API, but distributing an integration to multiple Zendesk customers requires a Zendesk-approved Global OAuth client. Additionally, Zendesk's MCP client requires Suite Growth+ or Support Team+ plans, while the Zendesk Bridge MCP server is currently in an Early Access Program (EAP).
api_surface_notes: Subdomain-scoped REST API (/api/v2/) supporting CRUD operations and sideloading across core support resources including tickets, users, organizations, help center, macros, triggers, and OAuth tokens. Rate limits, sandbox terms, and full endpoint catalogs were not detailed in the retrieved excerpts.
primary_blocker: Distributing a multi-tenant integration requires Zendesk approval for a Global OAuth client (otherwise each customer admin must configure a subdomain-scoped OAuth client), and legacy API token authentication is being fully removed by April 30, 2027.

name: Intercom
one_liner: Intercom is a customer communications and support helpdesk platform offering messaging, ticketing, help center management, and AI-powered customer service.
auth_notes: Public multi-tenant integrations must use OAuth2 with regional auth hosts (US, EU, AU) and token exchange, while private workspace apps use Bearer Access Tokens; token access is also bounded by the installing teammate's conversation permissions.
access_notes: Free development workspaces are self-serve for building and testing, but public OAuth integrations must pass Intercom app review (with strict scope scrutiny), and custom MCP OAuth redirect URIs require a manual support allowlist entry.
api_surface_notes: REST API v2.18 covering users, contacts, companies, segments, tags, conversations, tickets, events, custom objects/attributes, admins, Help Center articles, newsfeeds, AI content, data connectors, and exports.
primary_blocker: Public OAuth integrations require Intercom app review and regional host routing (US/EU/AU), and third-party OAuth clients connecting to Intercom's official MCP server require support allowlisting for non-localhost redirect URIs.

name: Freshdesk
one_liner: Cloud-based customer support and helpdesk platform for managing tickets, conversations, contacts, companies, and knowledge base operations.
auth_notes: REST API v2 supports personal API keys and Service Account API keys passed via HTTP Basic Auth (Base64-encoded apikey:X) as well as OAuth 2.0 scopes; Freshworks' official MCP server currently supports API key authentication only and does not support OAuth.
access_notes: API keys and API functionality are not available on the free Sprout plan. Official MCP integration is GA on Growth, Pro, and Enterprise plans (Freshdesk Standalone 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026) with annual action allowances (1,200, 6,000, and 12,000 actions respectively) and per-minute rate limits.
api_surface_notes: REST v2 over HTTPS on tenant Freshdesk domains (custom CNAMEs unsupported; v1 deprecated). Covers tickets, notes, replies, outbound emails, contacts, companies, agents, groups, ticket fields, attachments, satisfaction ratings, time entries, search, service accounts, and knowledge base solutions, with an official JavaScript SDK (@freshworks/freshdesk).
primary_blocker: API access and keys are excluded on the free Sprout plan (paid plan required), API and MCP endpoints require tenant-specific Freshdesk domains without custom CNAME support, and the official MCP server lacks OAuth and enforces annual action quotas.

name: Front
one_liner: Front is a multi-channel customer operations platform that centralizes email, SMS, chat, and other messaging channels into collaborative team inboxes.
auth_notes: Core API requests use Bearer authentication via either OAuth 2.0 (authorization code grant; Basic auth is used only at the token endpoint, with 60-minute access tokens and 6-month refresh tokens) or company-level admin API tokens. Front's official MCP server supports OAuth 2.1 with PKCE using confidential client credentials (no Dynamic Client Registration).
access_notes: Creating developer apps or API tokens requires a Front company admin account (Settings > Company > Developer), and end users authorizing Core API OAuth apps must also be admins (the user-scoped MCP server is the only exception). Public integrations distributed to all Front customers must use OAuth and be published in the Front App Store unless Front grants an exception.
api_surface_notes: The Core REST API (https://api2.frontapp.com) exposes conversations, messages, drafts, contacts, accounts, inboxes, tags, teams, teammates, and rules across global, shared, and private namespaces with granular read/write/delete/send permissions. Front also hosts an official Streamable HTTP MCP server (https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp) metered at 100/200/300 tool calls per minute on Starter/Professional/Enterprise plans; SCIM auto-provisioning is gated and requires contacting Front.
primary_blocker: Developer app/token creation and Core API OAuth authorization require Front company admin privileges, OAuth refresh tokens expire after 6 months and only rotate during the final 24 hours, and the official MCP server does not support Dynamic Client Registration.

name: Pylon
one_liner: Pylon is a B2B customer support and helpdesk platform for managing customer issues, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles, and support workflows.
auth_notes: The REST API uses Bearer API tokens (Authorization: Bearer <token>) created only by workspace Admins, with US (pylon_api_) and EU (pylon_api_eu_) regional prefixes, optional bot identities, and IP allowlists. The official hosted MCP server supports OAuth 2.0 and Bearer API tokens per developer docs, though a knowledge base article states MCP only supports browser OAuth.
access_notes: Requires a Pylon workspace with an Admin account to generate API tokens (no standalone free developer sandbox is documented); Viewer and Integration seats cannot authenticate to MCP, and the Pylon MCP server is listed on Professional, Advanced, and Enterprise plans.
api_surface_notes: Covers issues, replies, internal notes, accounts, contacts, knowledge base articles and collections, macros, tags, triggers, tasks, and projects, supported by official TypeScript (@usepylon/sdk), Python (usepylon), and Go SDKs, an experimental CLI, and regional REST/MCP endpoints (US and EU) with rate limits (429).
primary_blocker: REST API requires a workspace Admin to manually generate Bearer tokens (no OAuth2 flow for REST or free developer sandbox), requires US/EU regional base URL routing, and the official MCP server requires a Professional+ plan with conflicting docs on API-token vs OAuth-only auth.

name: LiveAgent
one_liner: LiveAgent is a customer support and helpdesk platform for managing tickets, multi-channel conversations, calls, and knowledge bases.
auth_notes: REST API v3 uses a scoped apikey HTTP header (distinct from deprecated v1 keys) and lists an OAuth2 accessCode flow in its Swagger spec; the official MCP server supports OAuth 2.1 (Authorization Code + PKCE) or profile-generated Bearer tokens (up to 10 active, 2-year expiry).
access_notes: Any developer can register a self-serve 30-day free trial account to access tenant-hosted API v3 docs, generate API keys, and test the MCP server; production MCP server access requires Business ($44-$59/agent/mo) or Enterprise plans and consumes a shared AI budget.
api_surface_notes: REST API v3 (plus official Swagger-generated SDKs and 33-tool Streamable HTTP MCP server) covers tickets, conversations/messages, contacts, agents, departments, tags, custom fields, knowledge base articles/categories, calls/SIP, chats, SLAs, reports, SSO, and WhatsApp replies; note v3 message posting requires conversationId rather than ticketId and docs are hosted per tenant.
primary_blocker: None

name: Plain
one_liner: Plain is a customer support and helpdesk platform built on a full-surface GraphQL API with an official OAuth-authenticated MCP server for managing threads, customers, workflows, SLAs, and knowledge sources.
auth_notes: Supports fine-grained machine-user API keys sent as Bearer tokens (Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx) and OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code apps (client-side with PKCE or server-side with client secret using openid and offline_access scopes). Plain's official MCP server supports OAuth only.
access_notes: Developers can sign up self-serve at app.plain.com/get-started to create a workspace, generate test threads, and provision machine-user API keys or OAuth apps in Settings without sales gating. Custom OAuth apps are scoped only to the workspace in which they are created.
api_surface_notes: Plain's own UI is built on the same GraphQL API (https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1), giving full platform parity across threads, customers, accounts, labels, SLAs, workflows, broadcasts, and Help Center resources. GraphQL subscriptions do not accept OAuth app tokens, and custom OAuth apps only work in the workspace where created.
primary_blocker: None

name: Help Scout
one_liner: Help Scout is a customer support and helpdesk platform providing shared inboxes, live chat (Beacon), knowledge base management (Docs), and support reporting.
auth_notes: Inbox API 2.0 uses OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code for third-party integrations and Client Credentials for internal integrations) issuing 2-day Bearer access tokens with refresh tokens. Docs API uses a per-user API key sent as the HTTP Basic Auth username with a dummy password. Restricted Docs callback auth uses signed JWTs.
access_notes: API access is self-serve on Help Scout Standard, Plus, and Pro plans via Your Profile > My Apps (OAuth2) and Security and Access (Docs API key), requiring an active non-Light user. Reporting API and Restricted Docs require Plus or Pro plans. No sales gate or mandatory app review is required to build integrations.
api_surface_notes: Inbox API 2.0 (api.helpscout.net/v2, HAL+JSON, 200 req/min and 12 writes/5s burst) covers conversations, customers, mailboxes, saved replies, users, teams, and workflows. Docs API v1 (docsapi.helpscout.net/v1, 2000-4000 req/10min) manages knowledge base sites, collections, categories, and articles. Also provides Chat API, Beacon, Inbox Sidebar Apps, and Webhooks.
primary_blocker: None

name: Gorgias
one_liner: Gorgias is an ecommerce customer support and helpdesk platform for managing tickets, customers, macros, automation rules, help centers, and AI support agents.
auth_notes: Public apps must use OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with Bearer tokens (24-hour access token expiry, non-expiring refresh tokens via offline scope, PKCE not enabled). Private apps and direct REST access use HTTP Basic Auth with user email and an individual API key.
access_notes: Private REST API keys are available on all Helpdesk plans for account owners and admins. Public OAuth2 apps require creating an app in a Gorgias Partners account (which yields draft Client ID/Secret) and passing Gorgias team app review to list in the App Store.
api_surface_notes: REST API routed per customer subdomain (https://{subdomain}.gorgias.com/api/) covering tickets, messages, customers, users, teams, tags, custom fields, views, macros, rules, events, jobs, integrations, satisfaction surveys, statistics, and apps. Postman collection is available; rate limits and sandbox details are not specified in retrieved docs.
primary_blocker: Public OAuth2 apps require a Gorgias Partners account and team app review for approval, all OAuth and API endpoints depend on customer-specific subdomain routing, and private API keys require a customer Helpdesk admin/owner account.

name: Gladly
one_liner: Gladly is a customer service and helpdesk platform centered around customer profiles, conversation timelines, AI guides/workflows, and external system lookups.
auth_notes: The public REST API uses HTTP Basic Auth with a Gladly user email as username and a user-scoped API token as password (requiring the API User permission). The Lookup API uses request signing, Public Answers requires no token, and Gladly's official remote MCP server uses OAuth2.
access_notes: No standalone free developer account or self-serve sandbox exists; sandbox environments (*.gladly.qa) must be purchased via a Gladly CSM or Support, and API tokens require a customer Administrator to assign the API User role. Official MCP access also requires enablement by the Gladly account team.
api_surface_notes: Documented REST API (v1.0) covers customer profile management, customer timelines, order data, organization info, Public Answers, and up to 50 webhooks, alongside a reverse Lookup API for injecting external data into Gladly. Full endpoint breadth is defined in the downloadable OpenAPI specification.
primary_blocker: No free self-serve developer sandbox (requires an active customer Admin to create an API User and generate a Basic Auth token, or CSM purchase for a sandbox); additionally, Gladly's official OAuth2 MCP server is gated behind account-team enablement.

name: Slack
one_liner: Slack is a team communication and collaboration platform supporting channels, direct messages, file sharing, canvases, lists, and app integrations.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth 2.0 v2 authorization code flow (oauth.v2.access for bot xoxb- and user xoxp- tokens, and oauth.v2.user.access for user-only OAuth/MCP flows) with PKCE and token rotation support; incoming requests from Slack are verified using a signing secret signature or Mutual TLS.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve create Slack apps and provision a free fully-featured sandbox via the Developer Program; admin.* APIs require an Enterprise plan, workspace installations may require admin approval, and the official Slack MCP server restricts access to Slack Marketplace-published or internal apps (unlisted apps are prohibited).
api_surface_notes: HTTP RPC-style Web API (https://slack.com/api/METHOD_FAMILY.method) plus official Slack CLI and JS/Python/Java SDKs covering messaging, channels/conversations, search, files, users, reactions, canvases, lists, incoming webhooks, and Enterprise admin endpoints; tiered rate limits apply.
primary_blocker: None

name: Twilio
one_liner: Twilio is a cloud communications platform providing REST APIs for programmable messaging, voice, verification, video, conversations, and AI agent communications across 30+ products.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 (Client Credentials and Authorization Code grants issuing short-lived Bearer tokens via oauth.twilio.com/v2/token), API Keys (Main, Standard, and Restricted via HTTP Basic Auth), and legacy Account SID + Auth Token via HTTP Basic Auth; credentials are region-specific.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve create a Twilio account to obtain an Account SID, Auth Token, API keys, OAuth apps, and test credentials, though specific channels like A2P 10DLC messaging and WhatsApp templates require carrier or Meta approval.
api_surface_notes: Exposes 1,800+ REST endpoints across 30+ products including Programmable Messaging, Voice, Verify, Conversations, Video, Flex, Lookup, Sync, TaskRouter, and Conversation Intelligence, with multiple API versions (such as v2010, v1, and v2) and regional endpoints.
primary_blocker: None

name: Zoho Cliq
one_liner: Zoho Cliq is a team communication and messaging platform offering channels, direct/group chats, bots, reminders, and workflow integrations.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth 2.0 via Zoho Accounts across 9 regional data centers with Authorization header prefix 'Zoho-oauthtoken', 1-hour access tokens, refresh tokens, and granular service.scope.operation scopes; integration components also support API tokens.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve register server-based, client-based, mobile, non-browser, or self-client apps in the Zoho API Console to obtain a Client ID and Client Secret with no app review or sales gate documented.
api_surface_notes: REST API v3 (with v2 backwards compatibility) covers channels, chats, messages, attachments, reminders, bots, incoming webhooks, message actions, users, teams, departments, organization settings, and datastores, plus a Postman collection; integrations must route requests to the user's regional data center via api_domain.
primary_blocker: None

name: Lark (Larksuite)
one_liner: Lark (Larksuite) is an enterprise collaboration and messaging platform providing APIs for chats, documents, Base tables, calendars, contacts, and approval workflows.
auth_notes: Supports RFC 6749 OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and offline_access refresh tokens for user_access_token (2-hour TTL), plus App ID/Secret credentials to obtain tenant_access_token or app_access_token; store apps additionally require an hourly event-pushed app_ticket and tenant_key.
access_notes: Developers can register custom or store apps self-serve in the Developer Console, but enabling scopes, sensitive permissions, and publishing app versions require enterprise administrator review/approval, and store apps require tenant activation.
api_surface_notes: Covers IM (chats, messages, members), Docs/Docx/Wiki, Drive, Bitable (Base), Contacts, Approvals v4, Attendance, and Auth (rate limit example: 1000 req/min, 50 req/sec on token endpoints). Note: open.larksuite.com and open.feishu.cn are separate domain environments whose apps are not interchangeable.
primary_blocker: Multi-token auth complexity (user_access_token vs tenant_access_token vs store app_ticket webhook), enterprise admin approval for app publishing/scopes, and strict Lark vs Feishu domain isolation.

name: Pumble
one_liner: Team communication and messaging platform for channels, direct messages, threads, file sharing, and calls.
auth_notes: The primary Integration API uses an OAuth2 authorization code flow returning non-expiring user accessToken and botToken values; every API call requires both a 'token' header and an 'x-app-token' (xpat-prefixed app key) header. A separate Pumble API addon also supports workspace-generated API keys via an 'ApiKey' or Bearer header.
access_notes: Developers and workspace users can self-serve create apps from scratch in Workspace Settings -> Configure apps to obtain app keys and OAuth/bot tokens, and the Pumble API addon is available on all Pumble plans to Owners, Admins, and Members without sales or app-review gating.
api_surface_notes: REST API at https://api-ga.pumble.com/v1/ covering Workspaces, Workspace Users, Channels, Direct Messages, Messages (CRUD, search, replies, reactions, drafts, scheduled, ephemeral, attachments), Files, Calls, and App Interactions. Rate limits are 100 req/min per user token and 500 req/min per app token (1000 req/min on the API addon), returning 429 with Retry-After.
primary_blocker: None

name: Discord
one_liner: Discord is a real-time communications and messaging platform for communities and teams supporting text, voice, servers (guilds), webhooks, and bot automation.
auth_notes: Supports Bot tokens (Authorization: Bot <token>) for bot accounts, OAuth2 Bearer tokens (Authorization: Bearer <token>) via authorization code, implicit, client credentials, and bot/webhook passthrough flows, plus Basic Auth (client_id:client_secret) on OAuth2 token endpoints.
access_notes: Any developer can register an application and generate Bot tokens and OAuth2 credentials for free in the Discord Developer Portal; privileged Gateway intents require review past 10,000 users and specialized scopes (e.g., dm_channels.read, rpc, voice) require partner approval.
api_surface_notes: Versioned REST API (v10/v9 active at https://discord.com/api) plus Real-Time Gateway for events; covers guilds, channels, messages, users, roles, slash commands, webhooks, and lobbies, with strict RFC 6585 rate limiting.
primary_blocker: None

name: Telegram
one_liner: Cloud-based messaging platform providing an HTTP Bot API for automated bots and an MTProto client API/TDLib for full Telegram client integrations.
auth_notes: The HTTP Bot API uses a bot token from @BotFather embedded in the request URL; the MTProto Telegram API requires an api_id and api_hash from my.telegram.org plus phone verification, QR code, passkey, or SRP 2FA login bound to an encrypted auth_key_id.
access_notes: Both the Bot API and MTProto Telegram API are open and free of charge for all developers; obtaining an api_id/api_hash requires an active Telegram phone number at my.telegram.org, and unofficial MTProto clients are monitored for spam/abuse.
api_surface_notes: Offers an HTTP-based Bot API (GET/POST with JSON or multipart/form-data) alongside the full MTProto RPC API and TDLib covering messaging, auth, accounts, and web login authorizations; MTProto methods are also listed in a JSON RPC db.
primary_blocker: None

name: WhatsApp Business
one_liner: WhatsApp Business Platform enables businesses to programmatically send messages and calls, manage message templates, configure webhooks, and administer WhatsApp Business accounts and phone numbers via Meta's Cloud and Business Management APIs.
auth_notes: Uses Meta Graph API Bearer access tokens: short-lived User access tokens for testing, long-lived System User access tokens for single-business apps, and Business Integration System User tokens (exchanged via Facebook Login for Businesses / Embedded Signup) for multi-tenant Tech Providers; requires whatsapp_business_messaging, whatsapp_business_management, and public_profile permissions.
access_notes: Developers can create a Meta App and test business account self-serve with temporary tokens, but production multi-customer usage requires Meta App Review, Business Verification, Tech Provider Embedded Signup onboarding, accepted Cloud API ToS, phone number verification, and payment setup.
api_surface_notes: HTTP REST endpoints on Meta Graph API (e.g., v22.0-v27.0) covering Cloud API (text, rich media, interactive/template messages, calling, groups) and Business Management API (WABAs, phone numbers, media, business profiles, two-step verification, webhooks). Key constraints include a 24-hour customer service window for free-form text, pre-approval for message templates, and dual business asset access grants for system users.
primary_blocker: Meta App Review, Business Verification, and Embedded Signup / Business Integration System User setup for multi-tenant production access, plus template approval and 24-hour messaging window constraints (and Meta's beta official MCP restricts supported clients).

name: Aircall
one_liner: Aircall is a cloud-based business phone and communications platform offering call management, messaging, and AI conversation intelligence.
auth_notes: Supports HTTP Basic Auth using a Dashboard-generated API ID and API token (Base64 encoded) for internal/single-account integrations, and OAuth 2.0 (Technology Partner flow with install_uri, redirect_uri, Admin-only consent, and non-expiring Bearer access_token) for multi-customer apps.
access_notes: Basic Auth requires an active Aircall customer account (Admin/Dashboard access to Integrations > API keys). Multi-customer OAuth requires applying to Aircall's Technology Partner program (or contacting marketplace@aircall.io) for client_id and client_secret.
api_surface_notes: Public REST API at https://api.aircall.io/v1 (HTTPS only) with 120 requests/minute rate limit per company (headers X-AircallApi-Limit, X-AircallApi-Remaining, X-AircallApi-Reset; higher limits available via support). Retrieved docs confirm /v1/ping, /v1/calls/search, /v1/oauth/token, and reference webhooksData in OAuth setup, though the full endpoint list was not included in excerpts. Official beta MCP is read-only for calls and conversation intelligence (requires Aircall AI add-on) and excludes SMS/MMS/WhatsApp.
primary_blocker: Multi-tenant OAuth credentials require Tech Partner approval (plus custom install_uri and Admin-only consent), Basic Auth requires an existing Aircall customer account, and Aircall's official MCP (https://mcp.aircall.io/mcp) is beta-gated, account-wide, and read-only.

name: Vonage
one_liner: Vonage provides cloud communications APIs for programmable SMS, voice, video, messaging (WhatsApp/RCS), verification, and business communications.
auth_notes: Core Vonage APIs use API Key + Secret via Basic Auth (Base64 header) or RS256 JWTs signed with an application private key (required for webhooks and ACLs on Messages/Verify); message signatures use SIGNATURE_SECRET, SIP Trunking uses Digest Auth, and Vonage Business Communications (VBC) uses OAuth2 (authorization_code, password, and refresh_token grants).
access_notes: Developers can sign up self-serve to obtain an API key and secret, receive free starter credit upon opening an account, and pay per request by topping up their balance in the Developer Dashboard.
api_surface_notes: Covers 24+ APIs including SMS, Messages (WhatsApp/RCS), Voice, Video, Verify, Conversation, Numbers, Number Insight, Identity Insights, Accounts, Application, Reports, Redact, Programmable SIP, Quality on Demand, Device Location Retrieval, and VBC Account/Extension/User APIs.
primary_blocker: None

name: Google Ads
one_liner: Google Ads is Google's online advertising platform for managing, optimizing, and reporting on paid ad campaigns across Google Search, YouTube, Display, and partner networks.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 user authentication and service accounts using the https://www.googleapis.com/auth/adwords scope tied to a Google Cloud project, plus a login-customer-id header for manager accounts; legacy developer tokens were sunset on September 9, 2026.
access_notes: Enabling the API in Google Cloud grants Test access (15,000 ops/day on test accounts); Explorer production access (2,880 ops/day) uses automated review in most cases, while Basic and Standard access require brand verification and Standard access enforces Required Minimum Functionality (RMF). Google Ads Developer Policies prohibit third-party hosted secondary APIs or MCP proxies unless end users use their own Google Cloud project credentials or the provider completes Developer Secondary Interface Review.
api_surface_notes: Supports full campaign, ad group, ad, budget, bid, asset, label, and customer account management alongside GAQL SearchStream reporting and resource metadata discovery; note that the official Google Ads MCP server itself only exposes read/GAQL tools and partial mutations (assets, video uploads, labels).
primary_blocker: Production scaling requires Google Cloud brand verification and RMF compliance, and Google Ads Developer Policies prohibit hosted third-party programmatic proxies or MCP wrappers without per-entity Google Cloud credentials or Developer Secondary Interface Review.

name: Meta Ads
one_liner: Meta Ads Marketing API enables programmatic creation, management, optimization, and performance analysis of ad campaigns, catalogs, and audiences across Meta technologies.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 user access tokens via Facebook Login (1-2 hour short-lived or 60-day long-lived) and Business Manager System User access tokens (non-expiring or 60-day expiring) with HMAC-SHA256 appsecret_proof for server-to-server calls.
access_notes: Developers can self-register an app and test in Graph API Explorer, but managing ads for external businesses requires Meta App Review for Advanced Access (such as ads_management and ads_mcp_management), app allowlisting, and ongoing Data Use Checkup and Data Protection Assessment compliance.
api_surface_notes: Broad Graph API surface covering campaigns, ad sets, ads, custom audiences, product catalogs, detailed performance insights (spend, CTR, ROAS, breakdowns), signal health diagnostics, A/B tests, conversion lift studies, activity logs, and programmatic MCP agent guardrail rules.
primary_blocker: Meta App Review for Advanced Access (ads_management and ads_mcp_management), allowlisting, Business Manager system user token handling, and ongoing Data Use Checkup / Data Protection Assessment compliance.

name: LinkedIn Ads
one_liner: LinkedIn Ads (LinkedIn Marketing / Advertising API) enables programmatic management of LinkedIn ad accounts, campaign groups, campaigns, creatives, targeting, and performance analytics.
auth_notes: Uses 3-legged OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow (and 2-legged Application Auth for select permissions) with granular scopes such as r_ads, rw_ads, and r_ads_reporting, requiring refresh token lifecycle management.
access_notes: Developers can create an app self-serve in the LinkedIn Developer Portal, but the Advertising API is a vetted product requiring an access application for Development tier (limited to manually mapped Ad Account IDs) and a video demo plus Technical Sign Off via LinkedIn Business Development for Standard tier.
api_surface_notes: Versioned REST APIs (api.linkedin.com/rest/...) cover all Campaign Manager capabilities including Ad Accounts, Account Users, Campaign Groups, Campaigns, Creatives, Targeting facets, and Reporting, with periodic version deprecations; an undocumented, gated first-party MCP endpoint (mcp.linkedin.com/marketing/mcp) was also reported via third-party probing.
primary_blocker: Vetted API access requiring LinkedIn app review for Development tier, a video demo and Business Development Technical Sign Off for Standard tier, plus strict integration compliance and recurring API version sunsets.

name: GoHighLevel
one_liner: GoHighLevel is an all-in-one CRM, marketing automation, messaging, and agency management platform.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow (24h access tokens, 1-year single-use rotating refresh tokens, no PKCE for Marketplace installs, split into Agency vs. Sub-Account tokens) and Private Integration Tokens (static scoped Bearer tokens rejected by OAuth-only endpoints). Requires a Version header (e.g., v3 or 2021-07-28); legacy v1 API keys reached end-of-support Dec 31, 2025.
access_notes: Developer Marketplace registration and Private Apps are self-serve, while Public Apps require HighLevel approval to be installable by all users. API access is available across paid plans (Starter $97/mo, Unlimited $297/mo, Founder $497/mo), with endpoints like Create Sub-Account and Enable SaaS restricted to the Founder tier.
api_surface_notes: Covers 38+ domains including contacts, conversations, calendars, workflows, payments, ad-publishing, affiliate-manager, agent-studio, blogs, businesses, and sub-accounts via https://services.leadconnectorhq.com. Versioned API (v3 latest, plus dated versions); Agency tokens can be exchanged for Location tokens.
primary_blocker: Public OAuth Marketplace apps require HighLevel approval, accounts require a paid plan ($97-$497/mo with Founder-tier gating for sub-account/SaaS endpoints), and OAuth uses split Agency/Sub-Account tokens without PKCE.

name: Mailchimp
one_liner: Mailchimp is an email marketing and automation platform offering REST APIs for managing audiences, campaigns, analytics, and transactional messaging.
auth_notes: Supports standard OAuth2 authorization code flow (non-expiring access tokens, no refresh tokens) for third-party integrations and full-access non-expiring API keys for single-account use; credentials are sent via HTTP Basic Auth or Bearer header, and requests require an account-specific data center subdomain (<dc>.api.mailchimp.com/3.0/) with no browser CORS support.
access_notes: Developers can create a Mailchimp account, generate API keys, and register OAuth2 apps self-serve without app review or sales approval; API capabilities depend on the account plan tier and user role, while Mailchimp Marketplace listing requires joining the free Integration Partner Program (OAuth2 + 25+ active users in the past 90 days).
api_surface_notes: Marketing API v3.0 covers audiences, campaigns, email activity, analytics/reports, and batch operations, supplemented by the Transactional Messaging API (Mandrill). Actions are bounded by the authorizing user's role (returning 403 if restricted), and an MCP-accessible API Use Policy restricts using MCP/API data to train AI/ML models.
primary_blocker: None

name: Klaviyo
one_liner: Klaviyo is a marketing automation platform for email, SMS, customer profiles, segmentation, and analytics with a broad REST API and an official MCP server.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with mandatory PKCE (S256) yielding Bearer access tokens (1-hour TTL, 90-day inactive refresh token expiry), Private API Keys (Authorization: Klaviyo-API-Key pk_...) for server-side /api endpoints, and 6-character Public API Keys (company_id) for client-side /client endpoints.
access_notes: Self-serve access using a Klaviyo account or test account with an Owner, Admin, or Manager role to generate Private API keys or create OAuth apps. Unlisted OAuth apps can be shared via installation URLs without review, while listing in the Klaviyo App Marketplace requires OAuth, least-privilege scopes, and 5 active installs.
api_surface_notes: Broad REST API under https://a.klaviyo.com/api/ requiring a dated revision header (e.g., 2026-10-15). Covers Accounts, Campaigns, Conversations, Catalogs, Coupons, Coupon codes, Data privacy, Events, Flows, Forms, Images, Lists, Metrics, Profiles, Push tokens, Reporting, Reviews, Segments, Subscriptions, Tags, Templates, Tracking Settings, and Web Feeds.
primary_blocker: None

name: systeme.io
one_liner: Systeme.io is an all-in-one marketing and funnel-building platform for managing contacts, email campaigns, sales funnels, courses, products, and automations.
auth_notes: Public REST API uses an account-level API key via the X-API-Key header (or query parameter), limited to 3 keys per account. The official MCP server uses an MCP key query parameter (max 2 keys, 90-day expiry), with OAuth2 planned.
access_notes: Developers and users can self-serve generate Public API keys and MCP keys directly in account Settings without sales approval or app review; the MCP server is explicitly included on all plans including the Free plan.
api_surface_notes: Covers contacts, tags, custom fields, newsletters, campaigns, email stats, funnels/page editor, price plans, coupons, courses/modules/lectures, communities, automation rules, subscriptions, webhooks, digital/physical products, offers, calendar bookings, and SMS templates. Supports cursor pagination and X-RateLimit-* headers.
primary_blocker: None (minor friction: no OAuth2 flow yet, so users must supply an X-API-Key with a 3-key-per-account limit)

name: Pinterest
one_liner: Pinterest is a visual discovery and social bookmarking platform that also provides advertising, catalog, and audience trend tools for businesses and creators.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code (for multi-user access with continuous 60-day indefinitely refreshable tokens) and Client Credentials (for app-owner M2M automation requiring 2FA). Token exchange uses HTTP Basic Auth with client_id and client_secret; API requests use Bearer access tokens with granular entity:read/write scopes.
access_notes: Developers register an app via a request form on developers.pinterest.com and undergo Pinterest review to obtain Trial access; offering full API capabilities to end users requires upgrading from Trial to Standard access. Additionally, Pinterest's official MCP server is currently gated on an invite/alpha basis.
api_surface_notes: Pinterest API v5 (api.pinterest.com/v5) covers organic content (public and secret Pins and Boards), User Accounts and followers, Product Catalogs, Ads (campaigns, ad groups, ads, reporting), Billing, and Business Access. Client Credentials tokens cannot access certain sensitive read/write endpoints.
primary_blocker: App review is required even for Trial API access and Standard tier approval is needed for multi-user production capabilities; additionally, the official remote MCP server is currently invite-only for ads workflows.

name: Threads (Meta)
one_liner: Threads (Meta) provides a social media API that enables apps to publish posts, retrieve profiles and media, read and moderate replies, manage mentions, search keywords, and access account insights.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow via threads.com/oauth/authorize and graph.threads.com/oauth/access_token with a Threads-specific App ID and App Secret; 1-hour short-lived user tokens exchange for 60-day refreshable long-lived tokens, and permission grants expire after 90 days unless refreshed (with private profiles previously restricted and now refreshable).
access_notes: Developers can self-serve create a Meta app with the Threads use case and test using invited Threads Testers, but granting permissions to non-role users requires Meta App Review approval per permission and publishing the app with required assets (icon, privacy policy, data deletion URL).
api_surface_notes: Served via graph.threads.com and graph.threads.net covering posting/carousels (250 posts/24h, media must be hosted on a public server), replies (1,000/24h), insights, mentions, keyword search, profile discovery, deletion, and 24h rolling call limits (4800 * impressions, min 10).
primary_blocker: Production access for external users requires Meta App Review approval per scope and app publication, alongside public URL hosting requirements for published media and 60-day token/90-day permission lifecycle management.

name: SendGrid
one_liner: Twilio SendGrid is a cloud-based email delivery platform providing transactional email sending, marketing campaigns, contact management, dynamic templates, and email analytics via REST APIs.
auth_notes: Uses long-lived API keys created in the SendGrid console (or via API) with Full, Custom (scoped), or Billing Access. Passed via Authorization: Bearer header for v3 REST APIs, or Basic Auth (username 'apikey', password API key) for SMTP and select services; Basic Auth is unavailable when 2FA is enabled, and no user-delegated OAuth2 flow exists.
access_notes: Developers can sign up self-serve and generate API keys in the Twilio SendGrid console (2FA is required for all users). Account Provisioning / Reseller endpoints are gated to formal Twilio SendGrid reseller partners.
api_surface_notes: SendGrid v3 REST API covers transactional Mail Send, dynamic templates, Marketing Campaigns (automations, single sends, contacts, lists, segments), suppressions, multi-dimensional stats and email activity, sender/domain authentication, subusers, webhooks, and billing (separate Billing Access key required). Official SDKs exist in 7 languages; accounts cap at 100 API keys and the on-behalf-of header does not work with Mail Send.
primary_blocker: None

name: Shopify
one_liner: Shopify is an e-commerce platform that provides GraphQL and legacy REST APIs for managing merchant stores, products, orders, storefronts, and customer accounts.
auth_notes: GraphQL Admin API uses OAuth2 (authorization code grant for standalone apps, token exchange with JWT ID tokens for embedded apps, or client credentials/signed client assertions) sent via X-Shopify-Access-Token; Storefront API uses public/private tokens, Partner API uses organization-scoped access tokens, and Customer Account API uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE.
access_notes: Developers can register self-serve for a Partner Account and generate API credentials in the Dev Dashboard, but public app distribution, restricted scopes, and protected customer data fields require Shopify approval/review, and client credentials grant only works within the developer's own organization unless using a public-distribution app with a client assertion.
api_surface_notes: Covers GraphQL Admin API (products, orders, themes, customers, store operations), Storefront API, Customer Account API, and Partner API; the REST Admin API is legacy as of Oct 1, 2024 and all new public apps must use GraphQL Admin API as of April 1, 2025.
primary_blocker: Multi-tenant public app distribution and access to protected customer data or restricted scopes require Shopify review/approval, new public apps must build on GraphQL rather than legacy REST, and API terms prohibit using merchant/API data to train AI/ML models.

name: WooCommerce
one_liner: WooCommerce is an open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin that lets merchants build and manage online stores, products, orders, and payments.
auth_notes: Uses Consumer Key and Consumer Secret over HTTPS via HTTP Basic Auth (or query string fallback for servers stripping headers), OAuth 1.0a one-legged HMAC-SHA1/HMAC-SHA256 signatures over HTTP, and an Application Authentication Endpoint (/wc-auth/v1/authorize) to auto-generate and POST API keys to an app callback URL. Official MCP integration uses WordPress Application Passwords (or WordPress.com OAuth for WooCommerce AI MCP).
access_notes: WooCommerce is a self-hosted open-source WordPress plugin with no central SaaS credential gate, paywall, or sales approval; any developer can test locally, while connecting to a merchant store requires the store's URL, non-Plain WordPress permalinks, and a WordPress user with sufficient capabilities.
api_surface_notes: REST API v3 (/wp-json/wc/v3/) is integrated with the WordPress REST API and supports JSON CRUD operations across core store resources like orders and products, plus /wp-json/wc/v3/payments/ when WooPayments is active. Official MCP integration (developer preview) exposes narrower purpose-built abilities for product and order CRUD and order notes.
primary_blocker: None

name: BigCommerce
one_liner: BigCommerce is an ecommerce platform offering REST, GraphQL, and MCP APIs to manage store catalogs, orders, customers, storefronts, B2B workflows, and payments.
auth_notes: Supports static store-level and account-level OAuth access tokens passed via the X-Auth-Token header (plus X-Store-Hash for B2B REST), app-level modified OAuth2 authorization code grant via login.bigcommerce.com/oauth2/token, and OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for Store Management MCP; legacy Basic Auth is deprecated.
access_notes: Developers can create trial stores or register immediately as a Partner to spin up a free sandbox store and generate store-level API credentials self-serve; however, distributing a public Single-Click OAuth app to arbitrary merchant stores requires an approved Technology Partner account and App Marketplace approval.
api_surface_notes: Covers Admin/Store Management REST (v2/v3) and GraphQL APIs (products, catalog, pricing, inventory, orders, refunds, promotions), Storefront REST/GraphQL, B2B REST Management, Customer Login/Current Customer, Payments, and multi-store Account GraphQL APIs; requests are routed per store hash.
primary_blocker: None for store-level token or official MCP integrations; public multi-store OAuth Single-Click App distribution requires Technology Partner and App Marketplace approval.

name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud
one_liner: Enterprise ecommerce platform providing headless storefront, catalog, merchandising, cart, checkout, and order management capabilities via Salesforce B2C Commerce APIs (SCAPI and OCAPI).
auth_notes: Split OAuth 2.1 architecture returning JWT Bearer access tokens: Shopper APIs use SLAS (authorization_code_pkce, authorization_code, client_credentials, session_bridge; private clients use Basic auth on the token endpoint and require channel_id for guest tokens), while Admin APIs use Account Manager client credentials via oauth2/access_token. OCAPI requires a registered client ID and OAuth/JWT tokens.
access_notes: APIs are included for B2C Commerce customers at no extra cost, but usage requires an active B2C Commerce instance (short code and organizationId), Account Manager administrative access, and SLAS Organization Administrator setup; no self-serve free developer account or sandbox signup is documented.
api_surface_notes: Covers nearly 600 SCAPI operations across Shopper APIs (products, browsing, baskets, orders, agents) and Admin APIs (merchandising, campaigns, promotions, inventory, jobs, custom APIs), plus legacy OCAPI Shop, Data, and Meta APIs. Exact rate limits are not detailed in the retrieved evidence.
primary_blocker: Requires an enterprise B2C Commerce customer or partner instance (Account Manager org, instance short code, and SLAS tenant configuration) to provision credentials and test integrations, alongside split Shopper (SLAS) and Admin (Account Manager) auth flows.

name: Magento (Adobe Commerce)
one_liner: Magento (Adobe Commerce) is an ecommerce platform offering PaaS, on-premises, open-source, and Cloud Service deployments with REST and GraphQL APIs for catalog, customer, cart, and order management.
auth_notes: PaaS, on-premises, and Magento Open Source use OAuth 1.0a (HMAC-SHA256 signatures via Admin Integrations) or Admin/Customer Bearer tokens; Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS) uses Adobe IMS OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens (server-to-server or user auth).
access_notes: PaaS and Magento Open Source integrations require merchant Admin access (System > Extensions > Integrations) and a store base URL; Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service requires an active Cloud Service license and Adobe Developer Console project.
api_surface_notes: Covers products, catalog, customer groups, customers, carts, and orders, but Cloud Service (SaaS) exposes a smaller REST subset (omitting customer/guest REST APIs in favor of GraphQL) and uses tenant URLs with a Store header instead of /rest/V1.
primary_blocker: Fragmented auth and API surfaces across PaaS/Open Source (per-store OAuth 1.0a HMAC-SHA256 Admin setup and custom store URLs) versus Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (Adobe IMS OAuth 2.0 and differing REST endpoints).

name: Squarespace
one_liner: Squarespace is a website and ecommerce platform providing Commerce REST APIs and an official remote MCP server for managing online stores, orders, products, inventory, contacts, and domains.
auth_notes: Supports merchant-generated non-expiring API keys (passed as Bearer tokens) and OAuth 2.0 with 30-minute access tokens and 7-day one-time-use rotating refresh tokens (requires access_type=offline and a User-Agent header).
access_notes: Third-party OAuth requires registering a client for Squarespace review to obtain credentials (a self-service developer-apps portal is also rolling out per Help Center), while API keys require a paid merchant plan (Core, Plus, Advanced, or Commerce Advanced); some Developer Tools APIs are invite-only.
api_surface_notes: Covers core commerce objects (Orders, Products, Inventory, Contacts, Discounts, Transactions, OAuth-only Webhook Subscriptions) plus Domains, Acuity, and invite-only Reseller/Scripts APIs; Forms API is Zapier-only and Profiles is in maintenance mode.
primary_blocker: Third-party OAuth requires client registration and review with 7-day rotating refresh tokens, API keys require paid merchant plans, Webhook Subscriptions are OAuth-only, and official MCP Commerce tools are currently limited to Claude and ChatGPT.

name: Ecwid
one_liner: Ecwid is an ecommerce platform by Lightspeed that lets merchants manage online storefronts, product catalogs, orders, customers, payments, and shipping.
auth_notes: Public apps use OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (via https://my.ecwid.com/api/oauth/token/{store_id}) returning a non-expiring Bearer access_token, public_token, and store_id. Private custom apps skip OAuth and generate non-expiring secret_token and public_token credentials sent as Bearer tokens; REST endpoints also require store_id in the request path.
access_notes: Free Ecwid stores cannot access the API (returning HTTP 402 NOT_AVAILABLE_ON_CURRENT_PLAN); custom app token access is self-serve once on a paid plan, though sensitive scopes require API Support review within 24 hours. Building a public OAuth2 app requires submitting an app idea request form (1-2 business days) for a free Premium test store, signing a partner agreement, passing App Validation with a screencast (3 business days), and having a registered corporate entity for AI-based apps.
api_surface_notes: Supports products, categories, variations, options, attributes, orders, abandoned carts, customers, customer groups, store profile/settings, store stats/reports, payments, shipping, and storefront customizations. Rate limit is 600 requests/minute per token (HTTP 429 with Retry-After). There is no API test mode; a separate test store is recommended.
primary_blocker: Public OAuth2 apps require Ecwid App Market submission, partner agreement, validation review, and a corporate entity for AI apps, while direct custom-app Bearer token access requires users to be on a paid Ecwid plan and manually supply store_id and secret_token.

name: Gumroad
one_liner: Gumroad is an ecommerce platform for creators to sell digital products, courses, memberships, and software licenses.
auth_notes: Supports standard OAuth2 authorization code flow (with client_id, client_secret, and granular scopes) as well as manually generated non-expiring Bearer access tokens from the app settings page; Verify License and public product JSON endpoints require no auth.
access_notes: Any user can create a free Gumroad account and immediately register an OAuth application or generate a personal access token in Settings > Advanced with no app review or sales gate.
api_surface_notes: JSON REST API (v2) rate-limited at 1,500 requests/min per token covering products, variants, offer codes, custom fields, files, sales, refunds, shipping status, license keys, audience emails, workflows, payouts, and tax forms, plus an official CLI.
primary_blocker: None

name: Amazon Selling Partner
one_liner: Amazon Selling Partner API (SP-API) enables sellers, vendors, and third-party apps to programmatically manage Amazon store listings, inventory, orders, FBA shipments, pricing, fees, and analytics.
auth_notes: Uses Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth 2.0 (refresh_token for seller-authorized calls and client_credentials for grantless operations) passed via the x-amz-access-token header with 1-hour expiry; PII endpoints require exchanging for a Restricted Data Token (RDT), and seller authorizations expire every 365 days.
access_notes: Developers can call sandbox endpoints without seller authorization while their developer profile is under review; production public applications require registering in the Solution Provider Portal, passing review, and obtaining seller OAuth consent via Seller Central or the Selling Partner Appstore (private apps can self-authorize up to 10 accounts).
api_surface_notes: Covers Catalog, Listings, Orders, Inventory, FBA Inbound, Pricing, Fees, Finance/Settlements, Tokens (RDT), Application Management, Tracking, and Notifications across regional endpoints (NA, EU, FE); requires user-agent and x-amz-date headers.
primary_blocker: Developer profile review and production app approval in the Solution Provider Portal, plus Restricted Data Token (RDT) handling for PII operations and mandatory 365-day seller reauthorization.

name: fanbasis
one_liner: FanBasis (rebranded as Commas) is a Merchant of Record ecommerce and creator payments platform for managing checkout sessions, subscriptions, invoices, customers, refunds, and discount codes.
auth_notes: Uses a single scoped API key passed in the x-api-key header with no OAuth or client ID/secret pairs; separate keys are required for production and sandbox, and webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 via the x-webhook-signature header.
access_notes: Any user can log into the Commas dashboard or the dedicated sandbox dashboard (sandbox.commas.net) under Account -> API Keys to generate scoped API keys immediately with no sales gate or app review.
api_surface_notes: Covers checkout sessions and embedded checkout, products, discount codes, transactions, refunds, customers, subscribers, subscriptions (including proration and upgrades under /api/seller/v1/subscriptions/*), invoices, and webhook subscriptions, backed by an official Stainless TypeScript SDK (@fanbasis/checkout-sdk); callers must use www.fanbasis.com because the apex domain 301-redirects and drops POST bodies.
primary_blocker: None

name: DataForSEO
one_liner: DataForSEO provides a suite of pay-as-you-go REST APIs and an official MCP server for accessing real-time SEO, SERP, keyword, backlink, domain analytics, business, and AI optimization data.
auth_notes: The v3 REST API strictly uses HTTP Basic Auth with a Base64-encoded API login and auto-generated API password (distinct from the dashboard login password, hidden in the UI after 24 hours and retrievable via email). The official hosted MCP server additionally supports OAuth 2.0 (Bearer tokens via RFC 9728 metadata) alongside Basic Auth.
access_notes: Any developer can self-register for a free account to receive a $1 trial credit (enough for ~500 live Google SERP requests) plus a free Sandbox returning dummy data, before transitioning to pay-as-you-go billing.
api_surface_notes: Covers SERP, AI Optimization, DataForSEO Labs, Backlinks, Business Data, and Domain Analytics APIs (over 80 endpoints historically) under https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/. Supports interactive Live endpoints and volume Standard async tasks with tasks_ready polling or postback URL callbacks. Potential account-level errors include unverified account (40104), optional IP whitelisting (40207), and low balance (40200/40210).
primary_blocker: None

name: SE Ranking
one_liner: SE Ranking is an SEO and marketing intelligence platform with unified REST APIs for large-scale SEO data retrieval (keywords, backlinks, SERP, domain, AI Search) and automated SEO project management.
auth_notes: A single API key authenticates both the Data API and Project API via the Authorization: Token YOUR_API_KEY header (or apikey/token query parameter). API keys cannot currently be scoped/restricted and belong to master accounts rather than sub-accounts. The official hosted MCP server also supports OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration or an X-Api-Key header.
access_notes: Developers can start with a self-serve 14-day free trial that includes 100,000 free API credits via the standalone API package without an active web subscription. Ongoing usage requires a paid SE Ranking plan (10,000-100,000 monthly credits included), pay-as-you-go credit packs (from $50 for 250,000 credits), an API add-on, or a standalone API plan.
