primary_blocker: Requires a paid Business, Enterprise, or Advanced Work Management plan for API/MCP access, plus OAuth Developer Tools registration approval and separate regional endpoints/tokens (US, EU, AU, Gov).

name: Harvest
one_liner: Harvest is a time tracking, expense logging, project budgeting, and invoicing platform for teams.
auth_notes: Supports OAuth2 (Authorization Code and Implicit Grant flows via id.getharvest.com) and Personal Access Tokens passed as Bearer tokens (or query param). All API v2 requests require Harvest-Account-Id and User-Agent headers.
access_notes: API access is included on all Harvest accounts, including free and trial accounts, with self-serve Personal Access Token and OAuth2 app creation in Harvest ID. API permissions mirror the user's account role.
api_surface_notes: REST API v2 supports GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE across time entries, timers, projects, tasks, clients, expenses, invoices and invoice payments, team assignments, timesheet approvals, and reports. Rate limits are 100 requests per 15 seconds (general) and 100 requests per 15 minutes (Reports API). An official remote MCP server is also available at https://api.harvestapp.com/mcp.
primary_blocker: None

name: Stripe
one_liner: Stripe is a financial infrastructure and payments platform offering comprehensive REST APIs and an official remote MCP server for managing payments, customers, subscriptions, Connect accounts, analytics, and Treasury operations.
auth_notes: Supports secret (sk_), restricted (rk_), organization (sk_org_), and agent-tagged restricted API keys passed via HTTP Basic Auth or Bearer token, Workload Identity Federation, plus OAuth 2.0 for Stripe Apps (1-hour access / 1-year rolling refresh tokens) and Stripe's remote MCP server (14-day max OAuth sessions or Agent API keys).
access_notes: Any developer can create a free Stripe account and immediately use sandboxes and test API keys (sk_test_, rk_test_). Accepting real money in live mode requires completing Stripe account setup, and publishing a public OAuth Stripe App on the Stripe App Marketplace requires Stripe App Review.
api_surface_notes: Broad REST API (v1 and v2) covering Customers, PaymentIntents, Refunds, Subscriptions, Billing, Connect (multi-account via Stripe-Account header), Analytics/Reporting, Atlas company formation, and Treasury. Isolated sandbox vs. live modes are provided, and agent-tagged keys or MCP tools enforce human confirmation approval rules for high-risk actions like refunds, payouts, and money movement.
primary_blocker: None

name: Plaid
one_liner: Plaid is a financial data API platform that connects applications to users' bank and financial institution accounts for transactions, balances, identity verification, and analytics.
auth_notes: Most endpoints require client_id and secret (via request body or PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers) plus a long-lived Item access_token obtained via Plaid Link public_token exchange. Plaid also offers OAuth 2.0 via /oauth/token (client_credentials, refresh_token, and token-exchange) issuing 15-minute Bearer tokens for Dashboard MCP and data-sharing services.
access_notes: Sandbox client_id and secret are self-serve upon Dashboard signup. Production access (trial or paid) must be requested and approved by Plaid, and connecting to OAuth-enabled banks or using the Dashboard MCP server requires Production approval, compliance center registration, and a security questionnaire review.
api_surface_notes: JSON-over-HTTPS POST endpoints across Sandbox and Production covering Link, Items, Institutions, Transactions, Investments, Asset Reports, Enrich, Identity Verification, Monitor, Protect, Document Income, and OAuth. Live bank connections require an interactive Link or Hosted Link flow to obtain a public_token, while Sandbox offers /sandbox/public_token/create.
primary_blocker: Production API access, OAuth bank institution access, and the Dashboard MCP server require Plaid approval, compliance registration, and a security questionnaire review, and live end-user bank connections require an interactive Plaid Link flow.

name: Binance
one_liner: Binance is a global cryptocurrency exchange and Web3 platform offering programmatic APIs for market data, spot and derivatives trading, account/wallet operations, and AI agent integrations.
auth_notes: Private REST and WebSocket endpoints require an API key (`X-MBX-APIKEY`) paired with HMAC-SHA256 or asymmetric RSA/Ed25519 request signing (FIX requires Ed25519). Binance OAuth and the official Agentic MCP Server use OAuth 2.0/2.1 Authorization Code with PKCE (S256) and client ID metadata documents.
access_notes: Public market data requires no authentication, and developers can self-serve API keys and test on free Testnet (`testnet.binance.vision`) or demo environments without sales approval. Live trading requires a Binance account, while specialized programs like Web3 DApp listing or Binance Connect partner APIs require application review.
api_surface_notes: Covers public market data, Spot, Margin, USD-M/COIN-M Futures, Options, Convert, Wallet/Account management, and on/off-ramp flows across REST, WebSocket APIs/Streams, FIX, SBE, and Streamable HTTP MCP. Enforces IP-based weighted rate limits (`X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-*`) that trigger HTTP 429 warnings and HTTP 418 IP bans.
primary_blocker: Requires per-request HMAC/RSA/Ed25519 cryptographic signing, faces HTTP 418 IP-based rate-limit bans on shared cloud egress IPs, and the official MCP server requires browser OAuth plus manual Agentic sub-account funding with no published tools/list schema.

name: Paygent Connect
one_liner: Paygent Connect (documented under Payman AI) is an API and MCP platform that connects AI applications and agents to customer bank and financial accounts for reading financial data and executing approval-gated money tasks.
auth_notes: Confidential server apps send an app key (x-paygent-connect-app-key) with a per-customer grant token (x-paygent-connect-grant) obtained via browser consent redirect and POST /connect/token; public clients and the hosted /mcp server use OAuth 2.1 with PKCE (S256) and Authorization: Bearer. Separately retrieved NMI docs show OAuth2 client_credentials and API key headers, but do not reference Paygent Connect.
access_notes: Developers can register sandbox (Durango demo bank) or live apps via the Apps console (90-day registration expiry requiring renewal), and public MCP clients support dynamic OAuth registration. However, docs state the Railway API is a staging deployment with no separate production launch, and no NMI-powered Paygent Connect docs were found.
api_surface_notes: The HTTP wire contract consists of a browser consent redirect (/connect/authorize), POST /connect/token, POST /connect/interact (and /interact/stream NDJSON), approvals polling, user-action, GET /connect/tool-definition, and GET /connect/apps/me. Grants expire after 90 days or 30 days of inactivity.
primary_blocker: API is currently a staging-only Railway deployment with no separate production launch, requires 90-day app renewals and human-in-the-loop approval polling, and entity identity is ambiguous against the NMI-powered hint.

name: iPayX
one_liner: iPayX provides a forensic FX audit API and MCP server that benchmarks currency transactions against live mid-market rates to detect hidden bank spreads and estimate overcharges.
auth_notes: Requires an API key (prefixed ipx_live_ for production or ipx_test_ for sandbox) sent as an HTTP Bearer token in the Authorization header; webhooks use HMAC-SHA256 signatures (x-ipayx-signature). The public MCP endpoint also supports unauthenticated access for up to 3 free audits per IP per month and unlimited rate lookups.
access_notes: Developers can sign up and generate API keys self-serve in the dashboard with free-tier MCP limits (10 audits/day per API key or 3 free audits/IP/month unauthenticated), while higher quotas and full forensic reports require self-serve paid plans ($99/mo Developer or $199/mo tier).
api_surface_notes: Covers a focused FX auditing surface across /audit, /rates, /audit/document, and /v1/score-config, plus 4 MCP tools (check_fx_mid_market_rate, audit_fx_transaction, compare_fx_sources, full_forensic_fx_report). Documentation shows conflicting base URLs (two Supabase Edge Function URLs and api.ipayx.ai/v1 marked 'coming soon' on /developers) and varying request schemas.
primary_blocker: Contradictory API documentation (multiple base URLs across Supabase Edge Functions and api.ipayx.ai, mismatched /audit request schemas, conflicting tier limits), paid gating on full forensic reports, draft API Terms of Service, and all core services shown as Down on the status page.

name: QuickBooks
one_liner: QuickBooks Online is an accounting and financial management platform offering APIs for accounting, invoicing, payments, payroll, and financial reporting.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow is the only supported protocol; API keys and HTTP Basic Auth are not supported. Uses company-scoped realmId tokens with auto-rotating refresh tokens (100-day refresh window), requiring a public HTTPS redirect URI in production.
access_notes: Developers can register self-serve on the Intuit Developer Portal and use free Sandbox companies with localhost callbacks, but production apps require HTTPS policy pages, public HTTPS endpoint/redirect URLs, and production app approval; Intuit's hosted MCP is invite-only for Intuit App Partner Program members.
api_surface_notes: Broad QuickBooks Online REST API spanning Accounting, Payments, and Payroll, covering 29 entity types with full CRUD/search and 11 financial reports (Balance Sheet, P&L, Cash Flow, etc.), as reflected in the 145 tools exposed by Intuit's official MCP server.
primary_blocker: Production OAuth 2.0 apps require public HTTPS redirect URIs, HTTPS policy pages, and production approval, while Intuit's hosted MCP server is invite-only with IP whitelisting and restricted scopes.

name: Xero
one_liner: Cloud accounting and financial management platform offering APIs for accounting, payroll, bank feeds, projects, fixed assets, and files.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow (PKCE supported for native and MCP clients; 30-minute access tokens, 60-day unused refresh tokens, and granular scopes for apps created from March 2, 2026) plus Client Credentials via Custom Connections (AU/NZ/UK/US only, closing to new apps December 1, 2026). API keys are not supported.
access_notes: Developers can register for a free Starter plan (Demo Company and up to 5 connections). Core supports up to 50 connections with a payment method, while scaling to Plus (1,000), Advanced (10,000), or Enterprise (unlimited) requires App Certification (10 customers) plus initial and annual Security Assessments for Advanced/Enterprise.
api_surface_notes: Official OpenAPI 3.0 specifications cover Accounting, Identity, Bank Feeds, Fixed Assets, Project, Payroll (AU/UK/NZ), and Files. Rate limits are 1,000 calls/day/org on Starter and 5,000 calls/day/org on Core+; Journal, XPM, and Bulk connection endpoints require Advanced+ plans and security/use-case approval.
primary_blocker: Scaling past 50 connections requires a paid plan and App Certification (and annual Security Assessments past 1,000 connections), alongside strict OAuth 2.0 token rotation and granular scope requirements.

name: Brex
one_liner: Brex is a corporate finance platform providing business banking, corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, bill pay, travel, and accounting integrations.
auth_notes: Supports customer-generated user/API tokens (bxt_...) passed as Bearer tokens and partner OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code Grant with optional PKCE, Client Credentials Grant for onboarding, OpenID Connect, rotating 90-day refresh tokens, 1-hour access tokens). Brex MCP also supports OAuth 2.0 with Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591).
access_notes: Customer API access requires an active Brex account where an account or card admin accepts the Developer API agreement and generates tokens on the production server (no standalone free developer sandbox). Multi-tenant partner OAuth requires contacting Brex developer support for a client_id and client_secret; Brex MCP additionally requires an admin to enable the beta feature.
api_surface_notes: RESTful JSON APIs covering Team/Org (users, roles, departments, locations, legal entities, cards), Transactions (card/cash accounts, statements, transactions), Accounting, Expenses, Reimbursements, Bills/Vendors, Spend Limits, and Travel. Note: granted scopes do not guarantee access if the user lacks the Brex role or underlying product; raw card PAN/CVV/expiration are excluded from MCP.
primary_blocker: No standalone self-serve developer sandbox (requires an active Brex customer admin account to accept API terms), and multi-tenant partner OAuth credentials require contacting Brex developer support, though BYO Bearer tokens and MCP OAuth DCR (RFC 7591) are supported.

name: Ramp
one_liner: Ramp is a business finance and spend management platform covering corporate cards, transactions, bills, reimbursements, procurement requests, approvals, treasury, and accounting automation.
auth_notes: Uses OAuth 2.0 at /developer/v1/token with Client Credentials (10-day tokens, no refresh token), Authorization Code (1-hour default tokens), and Refresh Token grants using HTTP Basic Auth for client credentials and Bearer tokens (ramp_business_tok_ / ramp_user_tok_ / JWT). Ramp MCP uses OAuth acting as the signed-in user with Full access or Read-only consent and 30-day connection expiry, while Ramp Data MCP uses a separate Ramp Data API key.
access_notes: Creating developer credentials self-serve requires a Ramp customer account with Admin access (Company -> Developer); non-customers must request sandbox access. Third-party integrations seeking multi-tenant production access must apply through Ramp's technology partnerships application, sensitive scopes like cards:read_vault require approved-integrator status, and business-wide OAuth authorizations require an Admin or Business Owner.
api_surface_notes: Extensive REST surface covering accounting, approvals, audit logs, bank accounts, bills, budgets, physical and virtual cards, custom records, departments, entities, funds, itemized receipts, payments, purchase orders, reimbursements, spend programs, transactions, transfers, treasury, trips, procurement requests, users, and vendors. Separate production (api.ramp.com) and sandbox (demo-api.ramp.com) hosts; token endpoint is rate-limited at 100 requests per 10 seconds per IP, and some endpoints require specific Ramp plan features.
primary_blocker: Requires a Ramp customer admin account or sandbox request to develop, a technology partnerships application for third-party production access, admin/owner consent for business-wide OAuth apps, and exact redirect URI allowlisting (with 30-day renewal) for custom MCP clients.

name: PitchBook
one_liner: PitchBook is a private and public capital market intelligence platform providing data on companies, deals, investors, funds, people, limited partners, and service providers via an enterprise REST API and an official MCP server.
auth_notes: The REST API uses a static API key passed via the Authorization: PB-Token {API_KEY} header with no OAuth flow. The official MCP server (https://premium.mcp.pitchbook.com/mcp) uses OAuth 2.1 (authorization_code and refresh_token with S256 PKCE) tied to customer SSO, requiring either partner allowlisting for Dynamic Client Registration or manually issued Client ID and Client Secret credentials.
access_notes: The REST API is a standalone paid, contract-gated add-on with no free tier and credit-based metering; production and sandbox keys must be provisioned via a PitchBook account manager or Direct Data team. The official MCP server (Premium Connector / PitchBook Data MCP) requires a qualifying PitchBook license, SSO, per-customer MCP enablement, and either AI partner allowlisting or a support-ticket OAuth client registration.
api_surface_notes: The REST API (https://api.pitchbook.com) exposes read/enrichment endpoints for Companies, Deals, People, Investors, Funds, Service Providers, Limited Partners, financing details, deal stock info, and VC exit predictor data, supporting X-Currency headers and credit-based rate/balance limits (402 and 429 responses). The official Streamable HTTP MCP exposes a subset of company, deal, investor, and fund lookups, though its full tool inventory is not publicly listed.
primary_blocker: Both the REST API and official MCP server are gated behind enterprise contracts, paid credit or seat licensing, and manual onboarding; REST keys require account manager provisioning and MCP OAuth Dynamic Client Registration is restricted to an approved partner allowlist requiring BD outreach or per-customer support tickets.

name: NotebookLM
one_liner: NotebookLM (Gemini Notebook API and Gemini Notebook Enterprise) is Google's AI research assistant for programmatically creating notebooks, ingesting sources, and managing sharing.
auth_notes: Requires OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens (API keys are not accepted). The Gemini Notebook API uses OAuth scopes (notebook, notebook.readonly) or gcloud ADC with x-goog-user-project; Enterprise uses Google Cloud IAM, ADC, or federated IdPs (OIDC/SAML 2.0).
access_notes: Gemini Notebook Enterprise (v1alpha) requires a GCP project, Enterprise subscription licenses (including free-trial), admin IdP configuration, and the Cloud NotebookLM User IAM role. The Public Preview consumer API (notebook.googleapis.com) is self-serve in GCP but blocks Google Workspace accounts (403) and requires prior UI sign-in (404 otherwise).
api_surface_notes: Official REST APIs cover notebook CRUD, sharing (Enterprise v1alpha), and source ingestion/upload/listing (v1), plus a 7-tool official MCP endpoint. Official docs do not expose chat/Q&A or Studio artifact generation endpoints, which community wrappers access via undocumented cookie-based APIs.
primary_blocker: Split Enterprise (v1alpha IAM/license-gated) and Consumer Public Preview (blocks Workspace accounts and requires prior UI sign-in) APIs, alongside a narrow official surface missing chat/query and Studio generation endpoints.

name: Otter AI
one_liner: Otter AI is an AI meeting assistant and transcription platform that records conversations and provides transcripts, summaries, outlines, insights, and action items.
auth_notes: Split authentication model: the official hosted MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with per-user browser consent, whereas the Public REST API does not support OAuth and requires static Bearer API keys (max 2 per user) generated in Integrations > Developer.
access_notes: The Public REST API is restricted to Enterprise workspaces (requiring an Enterprise plan and contacting an Otter account manager if unavailable or to enable Super Admin endpoints), while the official MCP server is accessible on standard Otter accounts via OAuth.
api_surface_notes: Public REST API (api.otter.ai/v1) offers cursor-paginated read endpoints for channels, conversations, transcripts, summaries, action items, insights, outlines, and audio downloads, plus POST /conversations to import media files and Super Admin workspace endpoints (10 req/s rate limit). The official MCP server (mcp.otter.ai/mcp) exposes 3 read-only tools: get user info, search, and fetch.
primary_blocker: The Public REST API is Enterprise-workspace gated and lacks OAuth (relying on static per-user Bearer API keys capped at 2 per user), while the self-serve OAuth official MCP server (already wrapped by Composio's otter_ai_mcp) is strictly read-only with 3 tools.

name: Fathom
one_liner: Fathom is an AI meeting notetaker that records, transcribes, and summarizes meetings and connects meeting context to apps and AI assistants.
auth_notes: Supports per-user API keys via X-Api-Key header (scoped to meetings recorded by or shared with the user/team; no org-level keys), Bearer tokens, and OAuth 2.0 (public_api scope) with short-lived access tokens and single-use rotating refresh tokens requiring concurrency locking. OAuth apps cannot pass include_summary or include_transcript on /meetings and must use /recordings endpoints instead.
access_notes: API access (keys and webhooks) and the official MCP server are included on all plans, including Free. OAuth app registration is self-serve with credentials issued in about 2 minutes; marketplace listing and co-marketing are reviewed quarterly after reaching 20+ users.
api_surface_notes: REST API at api.fathom.ai/external/v1 covers listing/filtering meetings, fetching recording transcripts and summaries, downloading recordings, OAuth token exchange, and webhooks, backed by official TypeScript and Python SDKs. Global rate limit is 60 calls per 60s per account, heavy endpoints (transcripts/summaries) are capped at 30 calls per 60s (throttled to 5 during peak load), and recording downloads have a separate 30 calls per 60s limit.
primary_blocker: None

name: Consensus
one_liner: Consensus is an AI-powered academic research search engine and agent platform indexing over 400 million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed papers.
auth_notes: The REST API only accepts an API key in the x-api-key header (no OAuth or Bearer tokens). The official MCP server supports both API keys via Authorization: Bearer and per-user OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code with S256 PKCE via RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration; static confidential client_id/client_secret pairs require enterprise sales provisioning).
access_notes: Any developer can self-serve an API key on the Free plan (30 calls/month, up to 20 papers/call on REST or 10 on MCP, 1 req/s). Paid plans (Pro, Teams, Deep) unlock pagination, full-text access, citations/references (beta), and 500-2,000 calls/month; Enterprise unlocks custom limits and static confidential OAuth clients.
api_surface_notes: REST API exposes /v1/search (plus paid /v1/papers/full_text and beta /v1beta/papers/citations and /v1beta/papers/references) at 1 req/s on standard plans. Official Streamable HTTP MCP server exposes 6 tools: search, get_full_text, create_thread, get_thread, add_to_thread, and find_threads. Private user Library documents are not accessible via API or MCP.
primary_blocker: None (note: REST API is API-key-only without OAuth; MCP OAuth relies on Dynamic Client Registration with PKCE, whereas static confidential OAuth clients require contacting sales).

name: Reducto
one_liner: Reducto is an AI document processing platform that parses, extracts, splits, classifies, and edits PDFs, images, spreadsheets, and 30+ other file formats into structured LLM-ready data.
auth_notes: Users create an API key in Reducto Studio (or via an OAuth device-code flow in the CLI/MCP) and pass it as an Authorization: Bearer header; the OpenAPI spec uses SkippableHTTPBearer and docs note a no-key fallback for up to 5 pages per document.
access_notes: Free self-serve signup in Reducto Studio (or via the agent signup API which grants 15,000 credits) with immediate API key generation; paid usage is billed per page.
api_surface_notes: REST API at https://platform.reducto.ai exposing /parse, /extract, /split, /classify, /edit, /upload (100MB direct, 5GB presigned URL), async equivalents (/*_async), and GET /job/{job_id}, plus jobid:// chaining and 429 concurrency rate limits.
primary_blocker: None

name: Devin
one_liner: Devin is Cognition's AI software engineering agent platform offering autonomous coding sessions, playbooks, knowledge management, schedules, code scans, PR reviews, and repository documentation via REST API and an official MCP server.
auth_notes: Uses cog_-prefixed Service User API Keys (organization or enterprise scope) or Personal Access Tokens (PATs) passed via Authorization: Bearer <token>. Enterprise service user keys and PATs also require an X-Org-Id header on the Devin MCP server; legacy apk_ and apk_user_ keys are deprecated.
access_notes: Requires an active Devin account/organization (unlike the free DeepWiki MCP). Service users are provisioned in organization or enterprise Settings > Devin API (with default 30-day expiration unless set to Never), and enterprise PATs are disabled by default pending enterprise admin policy approval.
api_surface_notes: REST v3 API covers Organization (/v3/organizations/* for sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets) and Enterprise (/v3/enterprise/* for analytics, audit logs, user management, billing, infrastructure) scopes, alongside an official Streamable HTTP MCP server (https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp) exposing sessions, playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations, automations, code scans, PR reviews, and DeepWiki docs.
primary_blocker: Requires an active customer Devin organization account and manually provisioned cog_ API keys or PATs (no OAuth2 flow for external callers; enterprise PATs are disabled by default and require X-Org-Id).

name: higgsfield
one_liner: Higgsfield is an AI media generation platform for creating and editing images, videos, characters, and audio via REST API, official MCP server, and CLI.
auth_notes: The REST API uses a Key ID and Secret passed in the 'Authorization: Key <key_id>:<key_secret>' header (legacy 'hf-api-key' and 'hf-secret' headers are also accepted). The official MCP server and CLI authenticate via OAuth to a higgsfield.ai account.
access_notes: Developers can self-serve API credentials at open.higgsfield.ai without sales approval or app review, but must register a payment method and fund a prepaid USD balance ($5 minimum top-up). Official MCP/CLI use OAuth and deduct standard higgsfield.ai plan credits with no free generations.
api_surface_notes: Asynchronous REST API at api.higgsfield.ai supporting 50+ image and video models, idempotent job submission, status polling, cancellation, webhooks, cost estimation, file uploads via official Python/TypeScript SDKs, and 20 concurrent requests by default. Official MCP exposes additional studio tools like Soul character training, Upscale, Genjutsu, Ad Multiplier, Audio, and Asset Library.
primary_blocker: None

name: Mermaid CLI
one_liner: Mermaid CLI (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) is an MIT-licensed command-line tool and local Node.js wrapper for rendering Mermaid diagram definitions and Markdown code blocks into SVG, PNG, or PDF files.
auth_notes: The mmdc CLI, Docker image, and Node.js run() API operate locally with no authentication. Separately, Mermaid's hosted SaaS MCP server (mcp.mermaid.ai) requires a free Mermaid account via OAuth 2.1 or API token.
access_notes: Freely installable via npm (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli), npx, or Docker under the MIT license with no account, paywall, or review gate.
api_surface_notes: Provides the mmdc CLI and an unversioned programmatic Node.js run(input, output, options) wrapper backed by Puppeteer, with no public HTTP/REST/GraphQL web API.
primary_blocker: No public web API: Mermaid CLI is strictly a local CLI and Puppeteer-based Node.js tool, whereas remote agent rendering and diagram management live under the separate Mermaid Chart MCP server (mcp.mermaid.ai).

name: YouTube Transcript
one_liner: TranscriptAPI.com provides a REST API and hosted MCP server for extracting YouTube video transcripts, metadata, search results, channel feeds, and playlists.
auth_notes: REST API v2 uses API keys (sk_ prefixed) passed as Authorization Bearer tokens; the official MCP server supports both Bearer API keys and OAuth 2.1 (Dynamic Client Registration and Static Client Registration with scope mcp:access).
access_notes: Developers can sign up free for an account, generate API keys from the dashboard, and receive 100 free credits; subsequent usage is credit-based (typically 1 credit per successful paid call, HTTP 402 when exhausted).
api_surface_notes: Base URL https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 exposes 13 GET endpoints covering video transcripts (JSON/text, language priority), video info/metadata, YouTube search, channel resolution/info/search/videos/playlists/posts/sections/latest RSS, and playlist videos, with no write endpoints.
primary_blocker: None

name: Grain
one_liner: Grain is an AI meeting recording and notes platform whose public API and MCP server expose recordings, transcripts, AI notes, action items, clips, and workspace meeting intelligence.
auth_notes: Supports Personal Access Tokens (PAT, personal scope) and Workspace Access Tokens (WAT, workspace scope) as Bearer tokens, plus OAuth2 Authorization Code with PKCE (including Client ID Metadata Documents for public/MCP clients). Server-side OAuth client_id/client_secret must be requested manually from Grain, and workspace scope requires Grain verification.
access_notes: Personal Access Tokens and personal-scoped MCP access are self-serve on all plans including Free, with no sandbox (developers test against a live workspace). However, Workspace Access Tokens and workspace-scoped API access require a Business or Enterprise plan and admin permissions, and server-side OAuth credentials require manual issuance from Grain.
api_surface_notes: REST v2 API (requiring Public-Api-Version header, 300 req/min rate limit) supports reading recordings, transcripts, AI notes, action items, participants, tags, teams, and meeting types; uploading external recordings; updating metadata/sharing; and exporting video (MP4) and transcripts (JSON, text, VTT, SRT). Grain also hosts an official remote MCP server at https://api.grain.com/_/mcp supporting personal-scoped OAuth/PATs.
primary_blocker: Server-side OAuth2 client_id and client_secret must be requested manually from Grain, workspace-wide scope requires Grain client verification plus a Business/Enterprise plan, and no developer sandbox environment is available.
